item: NetworkManager 1.58.1-1ubuntu3+rogsleep1: real suspend and resume on the ROG with a hard-NFS reader
host: ROG laptop, kernel 7.3.0-nativehdr3, Wi-Fi (wlo1), four hard NFS 4.1 mounts with nconnect=8

installed.libnm0:i386: 1.58.1-1ubuntu3+rogsleep1 (native i386 build in a debootstrap chroot, nocheck; Multi-Arch: same shared files byte-identical to amd64)
installed.transaction: 4 upgraded, 0 removed, dpkg --audit clean; stock 1.58.1-1ubuntu3 packages retained for rollback

procedure: Buffered dd from the middle of a 20 GB file on the media NFS mount; reader in folio_wait_bit_common; RTC alarm 75 s; systemctl suspend (the normal logind PrepareForSleep path); NetworkManager SUSPEND logging at DEBUG for the run, then restored.

results.networkmanager: sleep: device wlo1 carries a network filesystem, skipping
kernel: Freezing user space processes completed (elapsed 0.025 seconds)
Freezing remaining freezable tasks completed (elapsed 0.001 seconds)
results.sleep: systemd-sleep performed 'suspend' and returned on the RTC alarm after about 78 s wall time
results.wake: wlo1 re-checked as designed (activated -> unmanaged -> disconnected -> activated with a new DHCP lease) and connected about 5 s after wake
results.reader: alive after resume; read_bytes 169889792 -> 271601664 over 5 s

baseline: On November 13 the same kind of reader with stock NetworkManager made the freezer fail twice with -EBUSY and no sleep.
limits: One suspend cycle, one reader, digital records only; no long-duration or repeated-cycle soak.
